results.title: Christmas Charades Printable, 96 Act, Draw-It and Hum Party Cards for Families · HB-55
results.description:
Christmas Charades is a printable party game for the whole family: 96 illustrated cards in three modes and three levels. Draw a card, then act it out, draw it or hum it while your team races the clock. Every card shows its mode by color and shape (red burst = act, green sketch frame = draw, gold circle = hum), so even pre-readers know what to do. Original art by Hyperbox Prints, light on ink, ready in 15 minutes.

INSTANT DOWNLOAD · Printable PDF in US Letter + A4 · Nothing will be shipped.

What's included
- Cover + one-page rules: the three modes with pictures, 4 steps to play, levels and house rules
- 96 illustrated cards, 6 per page, each with its own drawing:
  - Kids: 30 cards (12 act, 12 draw, 6 hum)
  - Family: 36 cards (15 act, 15 draw, 6 hum)
  - Grown-ups: 30 cards (12 act, 12 draw, 6 hum)
- 18 hum cards with titles of traditional public-domain carols (titles only, no lyrics)
- Race to the Star scoreboard: a tree track with 4 cut-out team tokens + a tally table for longer games
- Paper hourglass table sign (cut, fold, stand) + a champion medal
- 20 pages in US Letter and A4

Who it's for: Families with mixed ages, Christmas Eve and holiday parties, classrooms before winter break, grandparents' visits and friend groups. Kids cards are picture-led (a grown-up can read along); grown-ups cards bring the holiday chaos. 2 to 4 teams.

How it works
1. Print the levels you want on cardstock and cut on the dashed lines.
2. Split into 2 to 4 teams. A player draws a card and acts it, draws it on scrap paper or hums it. The team has 60 seconds (use a phone or kitchen timer).
3. Each right guess moves your team token one ornament up the tree. First team to the star wins.

Sizes included: US Letter (8.5 x 11 in) and A4 (210 x 297 mm), high-resolution PDF. Every page has print-safe margins for home printers.

Printing tip: Print at 100% / Actual size. Use cardstock (65-110 lb) for the cards, tokens and hourglass sign. Light backgrounds keep ink use low. The paper hourglass is a decorative table sign; time each turn with a phone, oven or kitchen timer.

Digital download, nothing ships: This is an instant digital download. No physical item will be sent. Your files are ready on Etsy as soon as your payment is confirmed.

About the art: every illustration (Juniper the fox, the family, the 96 card drawings) was drawn for this game by our studio. No stock clip art.

Lights Out in Cedar Hollow is a printable murder mystery party for 6 suspects (the host can join in as a witness), with room for up to 8 more guests as witnesses and townsfolk. Download, print at home, play tonight.

The same opening is printed to read aloud. • Only the killer lies. Everyone else may dodge a question once, but must answer a second direct ask truthfully — so careful questioning really does crack the case. • Logic-checked. The solution follows from the evidence alone; we ran the full case through solver tests so no guess is needed and no innocent is framed by accident. • Two photo clues. A snapshot taken the moment the lights dipped — and an enlargement that changes everything.

Nothing will be shipped. • Print at 100 % / "actual size" on any home printer; cut the cards and name tags. • For your own private party — print as many copies as your party needs. Christmas Eve, 1960. Live on air. Someone in this studio is a killer.

A printable murder mystery party for 4 to 20 players, and the host plays too: the killer is drawn at your party, so nobody knows who did it, not even you. Instant download, US Letter and A4, phone and TV friendly.

⚡ INSTANT DOWNLOAD, NO SHIPPING

Channel 7's beloved "Mr. Christmas", Rex Harmon, raises his famous mug of cocoa on live television, says "Merry Christmas, America!", and two minutes later he is dead. Your guests are the cast and crew of The Starlight Christmas Hour: the co-host, the producer, the sponsor's man, the props master, the studio Santa, the gossip columnist and more. Everyone has a secret. One of them did it.

Story, documents and puzzles designed by me with AI-assisted tools; the photographs and portraits are AI-generated images.

🎬 WHY THIS PARTY
• The host plays too: three possible killers, and fate decides at the party which one it is. Even the host finds out at the reveal.
• Three different endings (Gold Star, Silver Bell, Red Candle): play it again with the same friends.
• Fair and solvable: every ending is proven by printed evidence, not by guessing.
• No filler roles: all 20 characters have a secret, two goals, a move in each act and something to find out.
• Easy to host: a one-page quick start, a TV Mode slideshow and six Channel 7 videos run the night with you.
• Clean and office-safe. Gender-flexible names for every role.

📦 WHAT YOU GET (5 files)
• START HERE (PDF): host guide, quick start, casting table
• Print Kit, US Letter (ZIP) and Print Kit, A4 (ZIP), each in full color and ink saver:
  – 20 character sheets with fillable PLAYED BY name boxes
  – secret cards for every act
  – Envelope 1, plus Envelopes 2 and 3 for all three fates (sealed)
  – the sealed reveals, read aloud by the host
  – party kit: invitations, fate tokens, envelope labels, place cards, menu card, accusation slips, awards
  – BONUS: Case Zero, a five-minute warm-up mystery
• Phone Kit (ZIP): every guest's sheets as separate files to send by phone or email, with password-locked act cards
• TV and Online Kit (ZIP): TV Mode slideshows, six Channel 7 videos and video-call backgrounds for playing online

🧩 HOW IT WORKS
1. Pick characters 1 up to your number of guests and send each guest their character sheet.
2. Print the night (or use phones), put each envelope in a plain envelope and seal it.
3. At the party, draw the fate token: it secretly decides the killer.
4. Three acts of about half an hour: open an envelope, read new cards, question each other.
5. Everyone accuses: who, how and why. Open the sealed reveal and find out. Hand out the awards.

ℹ️ GOOD TO KNOW
• 4 to 20 players, the host included. Characters 1 to 4 always play. Ages 12 and up.
• About 2 to 2.5 hours with food; about 1.5 hours with 4 to 6 players.
• Works in person, over video call, or mixed.
• You need a printer or phones, 8 plain envelopes, a hat and pens.
• Setting: a fictional American TV station in 1960. All people, places and companies are invented.
• Instant download: your files are ready right after purchase. Nothing is shipped.

🎁 GREAT FOR
Christmas parties, Christmas Eve, office parties, family gatherings, New Year's Eve, 1960s theme nights.

❓ FAQ
Can the host play?
Yes. The host gets a character like everyone else and only reads what the guide says is safe to read.

What if fewer guests come than planned?
Use characters 1 up to the number who showed up. Characters 1 to 4 must be played; everyone else is optional.

Do I need a printer?
No. The Phone Kit and TV Mode let you run the whole party without printing.

Black and white printer?
Fine. Use the ink saver folder.

Personal use only. Do not resell, share or redistribute these files.
